status_summary: The FCC element has advanced through program-by-program proposals, while the national strategy element has not. GAO testified on 2026-07-22 that no national strategy exists and that its 2022 recommendation to the Executive Office of the President to develop one has not been addressed. The FCC adopted proposed rules on Lifeline (FCC 26-8, published 2026-04-03), high-cost support (FCC 26-35, adopted 2026-05-20), E-Rate (FCC 26-41, published 2026-08-14) and USF administration (FCC 26-52, published 2026-08-31), all still at the proposal stage. The main final step found is the FCC's rescission of its 2024 E-Rate hotspot rules (effective 2026-02-20), on the ground that the statute does not permit E-Rate funding of off-premises hotspots. Amendments to the E-Rate competitive bidding rules (FCC 26-30) also took effect on 2026-09-14; they concern procurement and do not amount to a review of USF components. No single FCC review of all USF components was found.

timeline.event: The FCC's reconsideration order rescinding the 2024 E-Rate rules for off-premises Wi-Fi hotspots was published (effective 2026-02-20); it concluded that section 254 of the Communications Act does not permit E-Rate funding for off-premises hotspot use.
The FCC adopted a Lifeline and Link Up proposal covering duplicate discounts, costs, fraud controls and eligibility (published 2026-04-03).
The FCC adopted a high-cost program proposal that asks about overlap with unsubsidized competitors and BEAD (published 2026-06-05).

The FCC adopted an E-Rate notice of proposed rulemaking (FCC 26-41) reviewing the program's progress, its reading of the Children's Internet Protection Act, program integrity and administration (published 2026-08-14; reply comments due 2026-11-12).

GAO testimony GAO-26-109297 stated that no national strategy exists for federal broadband efforts and that its 2022 recommendation to the Executive Office of the President, through the National Economic Council, had not been addressed.
The FCC adopted a proposal on Universal Service Fund administration covering USAC oversight, audits, a possible budget cap and administrator structure (published 2026-08-31).

The FCC announced that amendments to its E-Rate competitive bidding rules adopted in FCC 26-30 (published 2026-05-19 at 91 FR 29051) took effect on 2026-09-14, after OMB approval of the related information collection (91 FR 58027).

title: Adopt a national broadband strategy and review FCC broadband programs including USF
uncertainties: The Federal Register documents were read in part and in summarized form (the Lifeline and E-Rate documents were read only to about character 100,000 of 137,000), so savings estimates in their later sections were not seen. The hotspot rescission order's adoption date was not confirmed, so the record dates it by publication; the Federal Register abstract gives a statutory ground, and the researcher's partial read also found cost and overlap with other federal hotspot programs mentioned. The GAO status page for the 2022 recommendation was read as open and partially addressed as of April 2024 and as not addressed in the 2026 report; the GAO recommendation database itself was not opened. The PLAN for Broadband Act status comes from the 2026 GAO report's description (subcommittee consideration) and a 2024 trade article about an earlier Congress, so its current bill number was not confirmed. No White House or NTIA national strategy document was found in two searches and the GAO text (a Benton Institute blog post, a lead only, also described none). These FCC proceedings are not linked to a White House request to the FCC; the Mandate's text frames the review as an Administration ask, and whether any such request occurred was not found. The FCC's general rules-deletion review and USF contribution base are treated in other records. Whether the Lifeline, high-cost and E-Rate proposals suffice as the review requested is a judgment. The Federal Register abstract of the E-Rate proposal does not mention BEAD; the researcher's partial read reported a question on overlap with BEAD and other federal funding, which the reviewer did not confirm, so it was removed from the summary. The 2026-09-14 competitive bidding rule was read only through its Federal Register abstract, which describes the effective date of earlier amendatory instructions and an information collection approval; its substance was not read. Federal Register comment dates were confirmed: Lifeline replies due 2026-06-02, high-cost replies due 2026-09-03, E-Rate replies due 2026-11-12, USF administration replies due 2026-10-30. No final rule from the four proposals was found in FCC documents published through 2026-10-18.
